Explore hourly bike rentals

bikehours-guide.Rmd

Compare peak rental times

Suppose you are a bike-share operations planner. You want to know whether casual and registered riders used Capital Bikeshare most heavily at the same time of day, and whether that changed on weekends and holidays. This example uses hourly rental counts recorded in 2011–2012.

Install and open the app

Install the package from GitHub. If the Classroom repository is private, you will need to use a GitHub account with access to it.

# Run once if needed: install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-asri0053")

Load the package:

library(bikehours)

Launch the app from your R console:

launch_app()

Explore the chart

  1. Select Working day and leave both rider groups ticked. Each line shows the average number of rentals at each clock hour across the recorded days of that type. Both groups reached their highest average at 17:00 (5 pm).
  2. Switch to Non-working day, which includes weekends and holidays. Registered rentals peaked at 12:00 (noon) and casual rentals at 14:00 (2 pm). The groups now peaked two hours apart.
  3. Untick one group to follow the other line on its own. If you untick both, the app prompts you to select a rider group.

Check a finding in R

You can reproduce the non-working-day result with the package’s summary function. Each row of its output represents one hour of the clock.

hourly <- summarise_hourly(bike_hourly, "Non-working day")

data.frame(
  rider_group = c("Casual", "Registered"),
  peak_hour = c(
    hourly$hour[which.max(hourly$casual)],
    hourly$hour[which.max(hourly$registered)]
  )
)
#>   rider_group peak_hour
#> 1      Casual        14
#> 2  Registered        12

For a planner, the comparison identifies when recorded rentals were highest across the system. The data combine all stations, so they cannot tell the planner which station needed more bikes at those times.
